text_excerpt: This Domain Has Been Transferred by Court Order — Radaris.com This Domain Has Been Transferred by Court Order Atlas Data Privacy Corporation, et al. v. Radaris.com, et al. Superior Court of New Jersey, Law Division, Middlesex County Docket No. MID-L-000847-24 Pursuant to a final judgment of the New Jersey Superior Court, the domain name radaris.com has been transferred to Atlas Data Privacy Corporation (“Atlas”) and is no longer under the control of its former operators. On February 8, 2024 , Atlas and five individual plaintiffs filed a lawsuit in New Jersey Superior Court: Atlas Data Privacy Corporation, et al. v. Radaris.com, et al. On May 27, 2025 , an Amended Complaint was filed. In the Amended Complaint, Atlas asserted claims assigned to it by approximately 21,760 law enforcement officers, prosecutors, and other “covered persons” under New Jersey’s Daniel’s Law, which protects home addresses and unpublished home telephone numbers from disclosure. On August 27, 2026 , the New Jersey Superior Court entered a final judgment by default against Defendants Radaris.com, Rehold.com, and Trustoria.com. The Court found that Plaintiffs “established that Defendants violated N.J.S.A. § 56:8-166.1, et seq., (‘Daniel’s Law’), as set forth in the Amended Complaint,” and awarded the seizure of this domain “to effectuate the purposes of Daniel’s Law to ensure the privacy and safety rights of covered persons.” The Court further awarded permanent injunctive relief “necessary to protect against and prevent disclosure, re-disclosure, or otherwise making available the home addresses and unpublished home telephone numbers” of the Individual Plaintiffs and Covered Persons, and ordered that Defendants and “all persons in concert” with Defendants are “permanently restrained and enjoined from violating Daniel’s Law, including disclosing, re-disclosing, or otherwise making available the Individual Plaintiffs’ and the Covered Persons’ Protected Information, including without limitation through: Radaris.com, Rehold.com, and Trustoria.com, as well as any subdomains, affiliated domains or sites within the possession, custody or control of Defendants, and any databases, computer systems, records or materials, however stored.” Additional information regarding the case and recent activity can be obtained from the Superior Court of New Jersey. For more information on Daniel’s Law and related enforcement efforts, see: Data Broker Radaris Loses Domains in Privacy Fight — KrebsOnSecurity (September 16, 2026) Study Finds Judges’ Home Addresses Remain Online Despite Federal Privacy Law — The Florida Bar News (September 10, 2026) US Judges’ Addresses Exposed Despite Privacy Law, Report Says — Bloomberg Law (September 3, 2026) Daniel’s Law Was Born From a Judge’s Family Tragedy. If you registered to vote anonymously , your details will not appear on either version of the electoral register. You will still be able to vote. How to opt out of the open register You can opt out of the open register. This is the version of the register that’s available to anyone who wants to buy a copy. To opt out, either: use the register to vote service (even if you’re already registered and live in the UK) contact your electoral registration office if you live in England, Scotland or Wales contact the Electoral Office for Northern Ireland ( EONI ) if you live in Northern Ireland contact the electoral registration office that confirmed you are registered as an overseas voter, if you live abroad Opting out does not affect your right to vote. When you opt out of the open register, your details will still appear on the full version of the electoral register, unless you’re registered to vote anonymously. The full version and what it can be used for Everyone’s name and UK address goes on the full version of the electoral register (unless you’re registered to vote anonymously), and you cannot opt out. This is the version of the register that’s used for elections and referendums. The full version of the register can only be used for: electoral administration purposes (such as sending out poll cards before elections) campaigning activities (for example, candidates and political parties sending election communications to voters, surveying opinions or fundraising) preventing and detecting crime checking applications for loans or credit jury summoning in England, Wales and Northern Ireland You can find out more about the difference between the open register and the electoral register on the Information Commissioner’s Office website . text_excerpt: Report an Error or Correction | Massachusetts Arrests Skip to content Massachusetts Arrests Find arrest records in Massachusetts Home Arrest records Warrant Search Inmate Search About Articles & Resources Login Report an Error — Massachusetts Arrests Public records systems move fast — counties update their portals, courts change their fees, and phone numbers get reassigned without much notice. Massachusetts Arrests works to keep every page accurate, but something may have slipped past us. If you’ve spotted a broken link, an outdated detail, or anything that just doesn’t look right, please let us know. A quick report from you helps every reader who lands on that page next. Maintained by MA Arrests Editorial Team · Verified 2026-06-23 What to report Almost anything that looks off is worth flagging. Common examples include: A link to a county or state records portal that is broken or leads to the wrong page A phone number, mailing address, or office hours that no longer match what an agency currently lists A fee or identification requirement that has changed since we published the page Information that conflicts with what you found on an official court or county website A typo, confusing instruction, or step that seems to be missing To help us fix the issue quickly, include the web address of the page you were on, a short description of what looks wrong, and — if you have it — the correct information along with where you found it, such as the official county clerk or court website. You don’t need to share your name or any personal details. Anonymous reports are welcome. Your name Your email Subject Your message (optional) What we can fix — and what we can’t We can fix anything that is wrong in our own guidance. A bad link, an outdated fee, a phone number that has changed, a step that is unclear — all of that is fair game, and the form above is exactly the right place to report it. What we cannot do is change, remove, seal, or hide an official record. Massachusetts Arrests is an informational guide. We do not hold or control any arrest, court, or jail records. Those records belong to the agencies and courts that created them, and only those bodies have the authority to alter or seal them. If you are trying to have a Massachusetts record sealed or cleared, that process runs through the courts — not through us. The legal avenue is called Expungement (and in some cases record sealing), and our Massachusetts arrest records guide explains how that process works and where to begin. If we have described that process incorrectly, please tell us and we will fix our description. But we cannot act as a step in the process itself. How we handle your report Every report submitted through this page comes directly to the MA Arrests Editorial Team. We do our best to review each one. When we can confirm an issue against the official primary source — the agency’s own website, a court portal, or a published fee schedule — we apply the correction. Most confirmed fixes go live within 48 hours. Some changes take a little longer when we need to follow up with an agency to verify current information. We genuinely appreciate every report. Accurate public-records information depends on readers who take a moment to flag what needs a second look. Thank you for helping keep this resource reliable. text_excerpt: Report an Error or Correction | Ohio Arrests Skip to content Ohio Arrests Find arrest records in Ohio Home Arrest Records Warrant Search Inmate Search About Ohio Arrests Login Report an Error — Ohio Arrests Ohio Arrests works to keep its county guides, office contacts, and process explanations as accurate as possible — but public-records systems change constantly. Fees get updated, county portals move, phone numbers get reassigned. If you’ve spotted something that looks wrong, outdated, or just confusing, please let us know. A quick report from you helps every other person who lands on that page next. Maintained by OH Arrests Editorial Team · Verified 2026-08-27 What to report Almost any factual mismatch is worth flagging. Common examples include: A link to a county or state records portal that is broken or redirects to the wrong place A phone number, mailing address, or office hours that no longer match what the agency actually shows A fee or identification requirement that has changed since we last checked Information on our site that conflicts with what an official county or court page says A typo or an explanation that is hard to follow To help us track down the issue quickly, include three things: the web address of the page you were on, a short description of what looks wrong, and — if you have it — the correct information along with where you saw it (for example, the official county clerk or court website). You don’t need to share your name or any personal details. Name * Email * Telephone Your Message What we can fix — and what we can’t We can fix anything that is wrong in our own guidance. A bad link, an outdated fee, a disconnected phone number, a confusing step-by-step explanation — all of that is fair game, and the form above is exactly the right place to report it. What we cannot do is change, remove, seal, or hide an official record. Ohio Arrests is an informational guide. We do not hold or control any arrest, court, or jail records. Those records belong to the agencies and courts that created them — and only those agencies and courts have the authority to alter or seal them. If your goal is to have an Ohio record sealed or destroyed, that happens through the courts, not through us. The legal process in Ohio is called Expungement (Destruction of Records), and our Ohio arrest records guide explains how that process works and where to begin. If we’ve gotten a detail about that process wrong — a waiting period, an eligibility rule, a court name — please do report it and we’ll correct our description. How we handle your report Every report submitted through this form comes directly to the OH Arrests Editorial Team. We do our best to review each one. When we can confirm an issue against the official primary source — the county portal, the court’s own page, or a state agency — we apply the correction. Most confirmed changes go live within 48 hours. Some take longer, particularly when we need to call or email an agency to verify a detail before updating it. We genuinely appreciate every report we receive. Accurate public-records information is only possible when readers take a moment to flag what needs a second look. Thank you for helping keep Ohio Arrests useful and honest. Data subjects in the United States and many other places have the right to opt-out from ad targeting, profiling, and sale/sharing of their data to third parties. When you select to Opt Out via a browser, we will attempt to place a non-unique cookie on your browser which tells our systems to stop targeting ads to that browser and to cease processing of data with respect to that browser. This opt-out also tells our systems not to profile, engage in ad targeting, cross-contact behavioral advertising or “sell/share” data. When you select to Opt Out of Eyeota’s use of a pseudonymous hash of your email address (HEM), we will place your HEM into an opt-out database that tells our systems not to to profile, engage in ad targeting, cross-context behavioral advertising or “sell/share” data associated with the opted-out HEM. Please note that you will still see advertisements online, however, these adverts may be less relevant because they won't be targeted by Eyeota based on your interests. We are a marketing company whose clients range from some of the biggest companies and charities in the United States to local charities, such as food banks. We help our clients identify people who might be interested in their marketing offers and help our clients analyze and improve their marketing practices. In other words, we create audiences and help our clients make better marketing decisions. To do this, we study consumer characteristics and then make predictions about the products, services and causes in which individuals are likely to be interested. We match those interests against the marketing goals of our clients to find the best fit. Sometimes our research is intended to help our clients find new donors or customers, and other times to find new ways to serve or connect with existing donors or customers. But whether they are our clients, the American consumer, or others, we care about people. This Privacy Choices page, describes ways that United States consumers can submit their privacy choices to us. We offer United States consumers the right to request to opt-out of our sharing of their personal information, the right to request that we delete their personal information and, for residents of states where access is a legal right, the right to request to access the personal information we store about them, as more fully described below. Airlines Reporting Corporation ("ARC," “us,” or “we”) provides a critical service in the air travel industry by providing financial settlement of transactions, including refunds and/or exchanges, between participating airlines and travel agencies (collectively, “Customers” or “Travel Providers”). ARC also provides data products, which are used by ARC’s Customers and third parties, to settle and report transactions, process credit card transactions, audit and reconcile sales data, and understand travel and demand patterns. This Privacy Policy applies to: information ARC collects, uses, and shares relating to individuals information ARC collects, uses, and shares at www.arccorp.com, myarc.arcorp.com, or other ARC-controlled websites, unless a different privacy policy is made explicitly applicable; and visitors to the ARC website. This Privacy Policy does not: Apply to how airlines, travel agencies, or other travel providers (“Travel Providers”) use or process Personal Data. It also does not apply to how a global distribution system or other travel technology company uses or processes Personal Data. Travelers should also carefully review the privacy policies of Travel Providers and global distribution systems; or Apply to information that ARC collects from job applicants or from ARC employees (which is covered by a separate policy). Personal Data We Collect In order to facilitate interactions with ARC and manage the business operations of ARC and its related entities, ARC may collect Personal Data and other information from different sources. These sources include: When you voluntarily provide us with the information; From your transactions with ARC’s Customers, including airlines, travel agencies, global data systems, or their affiliated businesses in connection with processing their travel-related transactions; and Other sources. "Personally Identifiable Information" (also referred to as "Personal Data" or “personal information”) is any information that identifies you personally, either alone or in combination with other information available from ARC. Personally Identifiable Information ("PII") does not include information that does not identify an individual. The types of Personal Data that ARC processes are a subset of the typical information that a passenger provides when they travel. This subset of information includes, at times, individual passenger name and credit card number and in certain limited circumstances, frequent flyer number, date of birth, and other identifiers associated with airline tickets sold to passengers through U.S.-based travel agencies accredited by ARC. Unless otherwise described herein, ARC does not collect or process sensitive personal data. ARC also collects technical information that does not directly identify a specific individual. For example, we may collect passenger name record (“PNR”) number and ticket number. As another example, when you use ARC's websites, we may collect information such as your IP address, browser type, the type of operating system you use, the name of your Internet Service Provider, and pages visited on our sites. When you use ARCs websites, this information is collected for site administration purposes such as monitoring and evaluating how visitors use the sites, analyzing usage trends and statistics, and enhancing the functionality and usability of the site to better tailor the sites, products, and services to visitors' needs. text_excerpt: Privacy Policy - The Collective Data Solutions The Collective Data Solutions Get Started Get Started Privacy Policy How do I remove my data from Collective Data Solutions LLC (“CDS”)? Visit the OPT OUT & DO NOT SELL page. Is the Collectivedata.io website intended for persons under thirteen years of age? No. The Collectivedata.io website is not intended for the use of persons under thirteen years of age. CDS does not knowingly solicit or collect personally identifying information (“PII”) from or about children, nor does CDS knowingly market its products or services to children. What is CCPA and how does it apply to me? Visit CDS’s CCPA FAQ page for answers to your CCPA questions. Is a website visitor able to access its PII? Yes. A visitor may request access to all of its PII. Does this Privacy Policy apply to linked websites? CDS neither owns nor controls the third-party websites; thus, this Website Visitor Privacy Policy does not apply to information provided to or gathered by them. What type of information does CDS collect from users of the Collectivedata.io website? By way of industry-standard web log files and similar tools, each time a user visits the Collectivedata.io website, CDS collects the URL from which the user visited, the pages visited, the computer’s browser information, and the IP address. Does CDS use web cookies on the Collectivedata.io website? Yes. CDS uses web cookies to track the pages viewed during each visit to the Collectivedata.io website. CDS uses this information to help improve the user’s experience and to better understand how users use the site. CDS does not attempt to link web cookie data to PII. Is a user able to block CDS from placing web cookies on its computer? Yes. A user may set its browser to refuse web cookies before accessing the Collectivedata.io website. In doing so, however, certain features of the site may not function properly and the user assumes all responsibility for any resulting loss of functionality. Is CDS a participant in the EU-U.S. Privacy Shield program? Yes. CDS is a participant in the EU-U.S. Privacy Shield Framework and Swiss-U.S. Privacy Shield Framework. CDS has certified to the Department of Commerce that it adheres to the Privacy Shield Principles. For more information regarding the program and its principles, visit https://www.privacyshield.gov/ . If there is any conflict between the policies in this Privacy Policy and the Privacy Shield Principles, the Privacy Shield Principles will govern. Does CDS collect any PII from website visitors? No, unless it is voluntarily provided by the visitor. CDS does not collect any PII when a user visits the Collectivedata.io website unless the user voluntarily provides such information as a result of: (a) submitting an inquiry through the Collectivedata.io “Contact” page; (b) submitting a request for a product demonstration through the “Request a Demo” page; (c) registering as a client on the “Sign Up” page; or (d) submitting an application for employment on the “Careers” page. Such PII may include, among other information, a user’s full name, physical address, email address, phone number, company name, and website URL. Users are under no obligation to provide CDS with PII of any kind; however, refusal to do so may prevent the user from using certain features of the site. How does CDS use the PII it receives from website visitors? CDS may use a visitor’s PII to: (a) inform the user of customized business solutions; (b) directly communicate with the user regarding the use of the CDS services; or (c) review a user’s application for employment. By using the forms found on the Collectivedata.io website, the visitor consents to the use of PII in order for CDS to contact and deliver information to them. Does the Collective data marketplace service sell personal information and what categories of personal information does it sell? The Collective data marketplace service collects the following personal information about you from third party data suppliers and has resold it in the preceding twelve months: Identifiers (device ID, MAID, IP address, hashed email); Commercial information (app activity); Internet or other electronic network activity information (browsing & search history, MAID, device attributes such as make, model, operating system); Geolocation Data (precise geolocation data, including latitude-longitude coordinates obtained from apps via requests to the mobile device operating system- note- the Collective marketplace service does not collect your precise geolocation in real-time); and Inferences drawn from any of the information collected to create a profile about the consumer (demographics, behavior and interests). What are the categories of third parties to whom the information was sold? The Collective data marketplace service has sold personal information to the following categories of third parties: brands, retailers, advertising agencies, financial institutions, data platforms and data brokers, and data analytics providers. What are the categories of third parties to whom the information was disclosed? The Collective data marketplace service has disclosed personal information to the following categories of third parties: brands, retailers, advertising agencies, financial institutions, data platforms and data brokers, and data analytics providers. What are the business purposes for which the personal information is collected, shared, disclosed, and sold? The Collective data marketplace service collected, shared, disclosed, and sold personal information for the following purposes: marketing, advertising, and analytics. How is my information used by the Collective data marketplace service? The Collective data marketplace service uses the information it receives from data suppliers to provide services to its clients. The Collective data marketplace service does not use information collected through its website to provide the data marketplace services. Using the information it receives from data suppliers, the Collective data marketplace service creates a portfolio of your device’s location data records which are associated with your mobile advertising identification number. The Collective data marketplace service tracks key performance indicators throughout the length of an advertising campaign and determines whether a MAID that was served an ad visited a particular store or location. The Collective data marketplace service creates insights and trends about consumer behaviors, including foot traffic at and surrounding a particular location and predicting future behavior. The Collective data marketplace service creates competitive consumer intelligence for clients, such as identifying new customers that may be interested in their offerings, targeting and enhancing marketing and advertising capabilities for clients. How does the Collective data marketplace treat information of minors under sixteen years of age? The Collective data marketplace service does not, to the best of its knowledge, collect or sell the personal information of minors under 16 years of age. What are some of the major rights consumers may have? Right to Opt Out: Consumers have the right to direct a business that sells personal information to third parties not to sell the consumer’s personal information. Cal. Civ. Code §1798.120(a) Right to Deletion: Consumers have the right to request that a business delete any personal information about the consumer which the business has collected from the consumer. Code §1798.100(a) Right of Data Portability: Consumers have the right to receive their personal information from a business in a readily usable format to enable the consumer to transmit the information from one entity to another without any hindrance. Superior Court of New Jersey, Law Division, Bergen County Docket No. BER-L-000869-24 The domain name corporationwiki.com is now controlled by Atlas Data Privacy Corporation (“Atlas”). On February 8, 2024 , Atlas and four individual plaintiffs filed a lawsuit in New Jersey Superior Court: Atlas Data Privacy Corporation, et al. v. Sagewire Research, LLC, et al. In the Complaint, Atlas asserted claims assigned to it by approximately 19,078 law enforcement officers, prosecutors, and other “covered persons” under New Jersey’s Daniel’s Law, which protects home addresses and unpublished home telephone numbers from disclosure. Atlas and Sagewire Research, LLC have entered into a settlement agreement, and this lawsuit has now been resolved. Additional information regarding this and other Daniel’s Law cases can be obtained from the Superior Court of New Jersey. Rather, our data consists of mobile device advertising IDs (“MAIDS”), cookies and hashed email addresses. To learn more about our data processing activities, read our full Technology Privacy Policy . Exercising Your Rights Datonics supports your ability to exercise your rights under applicable privacy laws, and, in our discretion, if you live in a location where no privacy law is in place that grants such rights. When you click on any request link provided below, we will automatically collect certain information from this browser on which you are viewing the form in order to process your request. Additionally, we will ask you for other information, including your email address, in order to validate and process your request. Please note the following additional limitations of using the Privacy Rights Request Forms: Web Browser Privacy Rights – If you choose to opt out, we will place a Datonics opt-out cookie on your browser and we will no longer allow the information we collect to be used for interest-based advertising purposes on the browser where you opt out. However, we are at the mercy of browser providers, such as Google Chrome, that may limit the amount of time a cookie can be active on your device and/or block our cookies altogether. If you delete cookies, use another browser or a different device, you need to renew your opt-out choice. Mobile Device Privacy Rights - Opting-out of processing your MAID will only be effective for so long as your mobile device uses that MAID. If your device generates a new MAID (for example, when you reset your device’s settings), your previous opt-out of the MAID will not be effective unless you actively opt-out again with your newly generated MAID. Email Privacy Rights - Opting-out of processing your email address will only be effective for the particular email address you entered in the opt-out form. To exercise additional rights such as the right to correct personal information or limit the use of sensitive personal information, please use the form below. Web Browser privacy Rights Datonics’ Browser Opt-Out Tool allows you to see the status of data collection on the current browser and exercise your rights to access, delete, or opt-out of sale or use for targeted advertising of your personal information pertaining to this browser. The Browser Opt-Out Tool utilizes cookies technology to store and access your opt-out preferences. This information includes Datonics’ Cookie ID assigned to your browser, your IP Address and your browser User_Agent string, and it is collected to only to facilitate the processing of your request. For the Browser Opt-Out Tool to function effectively on your computer with cookie-based identifiers, it's essential that your browser is configured to accept cookies. If your browser does not have cookies enabled or if you employ specific ad blockers, there is a possibility that our Browser Opt-Out Tool may not operate as intended. Additionally, if you decide to clear your browser's cookies, your opt-out preferences will also be deleted, rendering your opt-out ineffective until you actively opt-out once more. A plain email is your usual email address, like "example@email.com," which you use for sending and receiving emails. It's easy for humans to read. Plain emails contain the actual characters of an email address and are commonly used for everyday communication, online registrations, and various online services. They are easily readable and not encrypted or hidden in any way. A hashed email, on the other hand, is a jumbled-up version of an email address, created for security. It's like turning " example@email.com " into a secret code that looks like this: 542718bb7fad8057b5344e5e5f3a11303e618ac0262cc49313a03c9884fb914d . DataDelivers Privacy Policy Home Solutions Resources Insights Blogs Partners Home Solutions Resources Insights Blogs Partners Contact Us Data Delivers Notice of Privacy Practices and Policy Last updated and effective as of June 12, 2026 DataDelivers, LLC (“DataDelivers”, “us”, “we”, or “our”) is a Data Strategy, Analytic Insights, and Customer Management Technology company. We also operate the website located at https://datadelivers.com/ (the “Site”). We work directly with businesses to help them market, measure, and improve marketing campaigns across the direct mail, email, website, and social media channels. DataDelivers believes in a proactive, secure approach to protecting consumer privacy. Protecting privacy exists in every element of our business, from physical, virtual, and visual security to ongoing training for all our employees. Our related practices seek to balance the privacy expectations of consumers with the legitimate business need of our business customers. We also continuously seek ways to protect and assure appropriate use of information related to consumers and to promote policies within our industry that do the same. This Notice of Privacy Practices and Policy (collectively, the “Policy”) provides information about how we acquire consumer personal information on behalf of our clients, what types of personal information we store, how such information is used, and the rights and choices that consumers have about their personal information. The Policy is organized into two parts, with the first part addressing our general consumer data privacy practices and the second part addressing our online privacy practices associated with the Site. This Policy only addresses our data handling and privacy practices. Our clients may have different data handling practices which are not controlled by this Policy and you should seek out our client’s privacy policies to understand their respective privacy practices. Unless otherwise defined in this Policy, capitalized terms used in this Policy have the same meanings as in our Terms and Conditions, accessible from https://datadelivers.com/ General Consumer Data Privacy Practices How We Use Personal Information DataDelivers helps our clients’ market more effectively by understanding more about their clients and prospects. Client companies come to DataDelivers to understand their clients and prospects better, and our marketing technologies merge and link client and prospect data together and help in performing analysis so that our clients can provide more targeted and meaningful offers, messages, and customer experiences. Marketing Data Products and Services Our data products and services are designed to provide more insight and contact information on individuals and households in the US. Our marketing data products contain publicly available information, surveys, directories, and information from other data collectors. These products are used by businesses in their offline and online marketing programs. Our data products and service may include personal information, such as your name, email address, mailing address, telephone number, contact preferences, and other identifiers. We take consumer privacy very seriously. The obvious first step when looking up people online is to start with a reliable Google search. That alone can bring a lot of data to your phone or computer screen. Social media platforms, such as Facebook and LinkedIn, can be great places to learn more about someone. These social networks are a wealth of online information. You can also learn more about someone by searching public records databases and people search engines, both of which are free to use to some extent. Why Search For Someone’s Personal Information? There are many reasons you might want to search for someone’s personal information. Maybe you’re curious about an old flame, reconnecting with an old childhood friend, or a long-lost family member. Or perhaps you need to find contact information for a business associate. Whatever the reason for needing to find some information about a person, you can usually find what you’re looking for with a few quick and easy online searches. For example, you can use public records databases to find out someone’s address , phone number , and other contact information. You can also use social media websites like Facebook and search engines like BeenVerified , which help find people and their information based on what’s out there in public records. These are just a few of the resources to gather information online for free about someone’s personal interests, hobbies, and professional affiliations. In some cases, you can even use reverse phone lookup tools to find out the name and address of the person who owns a particular phone number. Some of these searches are easier than others, but you can find almost any personal information you need with a little bit of research. What Information Is Public & Legal? Before jumping in too fast to scour the web for all the info you can find, it’s important to have at least a basic understanding of what type of information is public and legal and what is considered private. If they do not have a nondisclosure agreement in place, the following types of information are generally considered to be public: Name Address Phone number Date of birth Age Employment history Most court records However, just because this information is publicly available does not mean that it is legal to share without consent. There are also other types of records that are considered private or semi-private based on circumstances, and these include: Medical records Juvenile records Some misdemeanors or civil violations Disability information Individual salaries (in most cases – salary laws can get complicated) So before conducting any online searches for personal information, make sure you understand what is and isn’t legal to share. Processing Your Personal Information FamousBirthdays.com is an open and easy to use platform. No user login is required nor offered on our website. We don't set any first-party cookies. Except as disclosed here, we don't track visitors to our site in any personally identifiable way. We automatically receive information from your web browser or mobile device. This information includes the name of the website from which you entered our website, if any, as well as the name of the website you'll visit when you leave our website. This information also includes the IP address of your computer (or any proxy server you use to connect to us), your Internet service provider's name, your web browser type, the type of mobile device, your computer operating system, and data about your browsing activity when using our website, including your search queries. We use this information to analyze trends among our users and to help improve our website. We do not use any personally identifiable information which could be attained by analysis of our log files, and our platform doesn't store any data or personally identifiable information about our users. Third-party advertisers may collect information on visitors to our site. More about our advertisers' data collection practices, privacy policies, and your rights with respect to advertiser data collection are provided in the " Third-Party Cookies and Sharing of Personal Information for Cross-Context Behavioral Advertising " and " California Consumers' Rights " sections below. Sale of Personal Information Famous Birthdays Pro sells information about the celebrities featured on our platform. This information is used by companies to help them identify celebrities for professional purposes such as casting or sponsorship. These reports include the Famous Birthdays URL of the celebrity, the Famous Birthdays ranking of the celebrity, and, when available, the celebrity's professional representation, public Instagram username, public YouTube username, public Twitter username, and/or public TikTok username. Famous Birthdays Pro also displays the historical rank graph for celebrities profiled on Famous Birthdays. Famous Birthdays does not otherwise sell personal information and we do not sell information about celebrities under 16 years of age. Profiled celebrities may contact us to opt-out of inclusion in Famous Birthdays Pro. First-Party Cookies Famous Birthdays does not use cookies to deliver content specific to your interests, and we don't set any first-party cookies to help deliver more targeted ads. Third-Party Cookies and Sharing of Personal Information for Cross-Context Behavioral Advertising Third-party advertising companies use your personal information to serve ads when you visit famousbirthdays.com and the Famous Birthdays iOS and Android apps. These advertising networks usually place cookies to develop a profile of your browsing interests and serve advertisements on other websites that are related to your interests. You will see less advertising if you disable these cookies. You can visit the Network Advertising Initiative for more information about this practice and how to use your cookie settings to manage advertising. For example, California has the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA). As explained further in our Privacy Policy, Faraday and our advertising partners collect certain pieces of information from our visitors, such as device identifiers, cookies, advertising IDs, IP addresses, and usage activity, so that we and our partners can deliver ads on other sites or apps. We and our partners may share this information with third parties to deliver relevant ads to you. This type of information sharing with our advertising partners may be considered a "sale" under the CCPA or other regulations. Also as explained in our Privacy Policy, we may share certain of your information with Clients and others. Below, we explain how you can control the information that is shared for online advertising purposes and with our Clients and others, and important information about those choices. Digital Advertising Alliance ("DAA") and Network Advertising Initiative ("NAI") Opt-Outs The Digital Advertising Alliance ("DAA") and the Network Advertising Initiative ("NAI") offer tools to provide consumers with choices as to whether participating third parties can use your information to provide targeted advertising. To opt out of sharing your information with such participating third parties for targeted advertising, please use the following tools: For websites: the DAA WebChoices Tool and the NAI Consumer Opt-Out Tool For mobile applications: the DAA AppChoices Tool Mobile ad settings If you no longer wish to receive interest-based advertising on your mobile applications, please refer to your device’s operating system settings. Information on "limit ad tracking" settings for many common operating systems is available on NAI’s Mobile Choices page . Please note The opt-outs described above are device- and browser-based. Because the information being shared relates to your device ID and/or browser ID, you must opt out on each device and each browser where you want your choice to apply. Opt-outs may be stored via cookies. If you clear cookies, your opt-out will no longer be valid and you must opt out again where you want your choices to apply. Faraday does not maintain or control the opt-out mechanisms and settings above and is not responsible for their operation. Exercising these choices does not prevent us from delivering contextual advertising, conducting cross-device tracking for us to serve you first-party ads directly, or using information for non-targeted advertising purposes, such as attribution and analytics. We may also still share some personal information with our partners to help us perform functions such as measuring ad effectiveness, controlling how many times you see an ad, determining ad performance, providing and securing ad, providing aggregate statistics and analytics, and/or reducing ad fraud. In such instances, these partners will act as our services providers. The above choices will not opt you out of the use of previously collected and shared information or all interest-based advertising (such as that conducted on other sites). Sharing opt out If you do not want us to share your information with our Clients and other third parties when such disclosure constitutes a "sale" under the CCPA or other regulations, please submit a request by entering your email below. Consumer request metrics California and other state law requires data brokers to report how many consumer privacy requests they received, and how quickly they responded. The figures below are grouped by the calendar year in which the requests were received. Received counts every request we got. The state columns count the unique people those requests matched in our records; requests that we could not place in any state are listed as state unknown. We comply in whole with every request: matched people are deleted, and for unmatched requests we hold nothing to delete. When we receive a request to opt out of sale or sharing, or to limit the use of sensitive personal information, we honor it by deleting the person entirely, so those figures match the deletion figures. Notes These numbers may include European requests under GDPR, however since Faraday does not hold or process European data, they will not be matched. In 2024-2025, Faraday received a very high volume of automated opt-out requests without accompanying authentication (that the consumer or their agent is who they say they are) and authorization (that the consumer truly gave permission to the agent). Faraday decided to honor these as deletion requests, but subsequently implemented stricter requirements which have led to a smaller volume of requests. In 2025, in response to identity theft concerns, Faraday started requiring (1) a scan of US Government Issued Identification, such as drivers license, passport, or ID card, and (2) a scan of a utility bill, lease, or bank statement with the same name as the government issued ID. text_excerpt: Delete vital information from Family Tree • FamilySearch How do I remove Vitals information in Family Tree? Article Id: 1288 August 05, 2025 Share Print You can delete vital information from an individual's profile, even if you are not the original contributor. You cannot delete some information: Name Sex Death information (unless you first change the status of the person to Living) Steps (website) Sign in to FamilySearch, click Family Tree , and then click Tree . Find the person that you want to edit. Click the person's name. In the details that pop up, click the person's name again. Click the Details tab . Under Vitals, find the information that you want to delete. Click the Edit icon . Review the current information and any reason statements. On the left side of the edit box, click Delete . If the box lacks a Delete option, you can only edit the information. Explain why you made a change. Click Delete . Steps (mobile app) In the Family Tree mobile app, navigate to the Person page that you want to edit. Tap the Details tab . Under Vitals, tap the information you want to delete. Review the current information and any reason statements. Tap Delete . If you do not see the Delete option, you can only edit the information. Explain why you made a change. Tap Delete . As a dedicated partner to our healthcare clients, protection of protected health information (PHI) has always been a priority. However, our protection of personal information extends beyond PHI to other personal information we may obtain or collect about individuals as part of our business operations. Please review our FinThrive Privacy Policy to gain an understanding of the type of information we may have and how we may use that information. State Privacy Laws Residents of some states have rights with respect to their personal information based on laws in those jurisdictions. FinThrive is committed to meeting our obligations to residents of those states and provide the state notices below to more fully describe how to exercise those rights. Rights provided under state laws do vary, but generally include: Right to know what personal information is collected/shared/sold Right to request that FinThrive delete your personal information Right to correct inaccurate information Right to opt-out of the sale or sharing of personal information Certain information may be exempt from such rights under applicable law. Other requests may not be fulfilled for various reasons, including, but not necessarily limited to requests where we cannot verify your identity or duplicate requests that have been previously processed. FinThrive will not discriminate against you because you exercise your rights. For example, we will not deny you goods or services or charge you a different price or rate for goods or services if you make a request under an applicable state privacy law. How to Exercise your Privacy Rights The privacy rights request process is reserved for residents of California at this time. By following the instructions provided below and submitting your request, you attest that you are a resident of California, or an authorized agent submitting this request on behalf of a resident of California. To submit a request to FinThrive to exercise your rights, please submit a verifiable consumer request via our Web Form , or call 1-877-636-5442. For additional information related to your rights and the Notice relevant to your state, please see: Notice for California residents Notice for California Job Applicants FAQs How long will it take to have my request fulfilled? Opt-out requests can take up to 15 business days to process. Access, Deletion, and Correction requests typically will be processed within 45 days but may take as long as 90 days. If we expect the request to take longer than 45 days, we'll let you know. Will my request be applied to all the information that FinThrive has received from me and other sources? No. The privacy rights provided under state laws exclude certain information such as certain health information, financial information, driving records, and consumer report information which are obtained and protected under other federal laws. Your request will be applied to all applicable information that we maintain. Change to Privacy Policy We reserve the right to change, modify, or amend our Privacy Policy and Notices posted on this page at any time. Therefore, we encourage you to review these documents each time you visit our website. Your continued use of our website, solutions, and continued interactions with FinThrive covered by the Privacy Policy and related Notices indicates your consent to the changes as of the last updated date indicated in the policy and each Notice. Third Parties to Whom We Share, Sell, or Disclose Information FOREWARN may share, sell, or otherwise disclose the information we collect to: Our Customers . Government, Law Enforcement, and Parties to Litigation . All Collections FAQs Compliance and Data Governance Do I need to update my privacy policy? Do I need to update my privacy policy? June 6, 2025 Yes! You should update your privacy policies when you start using Retention.com. To ensure best practices, Retention.com recommends you work with your legal team before making changes to your privacy policy. Please ensure that these changes are also reflected with a cookie compliance tool, such as CookiePro, to provide clear and transparent information to your website visitors. Here is the language you should add to your privacy policy: When you visit or log in to our website, cookies and similar technologies may be used by our online data partners or vendors to associate these activities with other personal information they or others have about you, including by association with your email or home address. We (or service providers on our behalf) may then send communications and marketing to these email or home addresses. You may opt out of receiving this advertising by visiting https://app.retention.com/optout . Please note that the language provided above is intended to guide you in updating your privacy policy to reflect the use of cookies and similar technologies by your online data partners or vendors. It is important to clarify that we, as your service provider, do not directly contact individuals on your behalf based on this data collection. The recommended text is to ensure transparency with your website visitors, indicating that they may be contacted by you or your service providers based on the information collected through these technologies. We encourage responsible and compliant use of such data in accordance with privacy laws and best practices. Related Articles How do I get started? What is email-based retargeting? These rights apply in certain U.S. States (California, Virginia, Colorado, Connecticut, Utah, Texas, Oregon, Montana, New Hampshire, Delaware, Iowa, Nebraska, New Jersey, Tennessee, Minnesota, Maryland, Indiana,Kentucky and Rhode Island), the United Kingdom, the European Union and certain other jurisdictions. The rights herein are only available to you if you are a resident of such jurisdictions and the laws of such jurisdiction apply to Intent IQ. These rights may include the right to access your information, the right to delete/erase your information, the right to correct/rectify your information, the right to opt-out of selling/sharing of your information, the right to opt-out of targeted advertising with your information, the right to object to our processing of your information, the right to revoke any consents, the right to limit the use of your sensitive personal information and other rights available under applicable laws and/or as set forth in our Technology Privacy Policy . Please keep in mind that Intent IQ’s products and services do not include the collection and use of identifiable information such as your name, physical address or unhashed email address. Rather, Intent IQ’s data is used to identify a device and may consist of mobile device IDs (such as advertising IDs a/k/a “MAIDS”), cookies, IP addresses, user agents and hashed email addresses. We generally do not create targeting segments or make advertising targeting decisions based on your data. Rather, our primary business is to enable others, such as our clients, to make their own targeting decisions based upon the sites and services that you have accessed online. To learn more about our data processing activities, please see our Technology Privacy Policy. EXERCISING RIGHTS * :Intent IQ uses, sells and shares the information we possess so that more relevant ads and other services can be delivered to you by third parties. While this information may be directly tied to your individual device (such as a computer or mobile device), this information may be “probabilistically” tied to your device. This means that we believe the information is tied to your device, but it may in fact be tied to other devices. Therefore, when you opt-out using the method below, it is possible that we will be opting out other devices in addition to yours that are on the same computer network with you. Opt-out of selling, sharing or targeted advertising with your information & delete your personal information: If you click the buttons below, you will be able to opt-out of the selling, sharing or targeted advertising with the personal information that we possess, and we will also delete such information, which we believe is tied to your device. Opt-Out via Browser/Cookie Opt-Out via Mobile Device Opt-Out via Email Access your personal information: If you click the buttons below, you will be able to see the personal information that we possess which we believe is tied to your device. Information about your browser Information about your mobile device Delete (limit use) of location data: As described in our Technology Privacy Policy, we may collect a limited amount of precise geolocation data, which is considered sensitive data under many laws. If you would like to limit the use of such data and have us delete such data, then please reach out via email to privacy@intentiq.com . Correction and Other Rights: You may have additional rights, such as the right to correct your information. Our information is generally not the type of information that you can (or would want) to correct. For more information about correction, please send us an email at privacy@intentiq.com . Authorized Agents: If you are an authorized agent of a data subject with the right under applicable law to submit a request on behalf of such data subject, then please send us evidence of such authorization via email at privacy@intentiq.com . Questions : If you have any questions, please send us an email at privacy@intentiq.com . * Please note that you will need to repeat these processes on every browser on every device you wish to delete or opt out, and if you change your browser (e.g., from Firefox to Chrome) or device, you will need to repeat these steps again. ** While IIQ provides the technical means for our clients to receive notification of deleted data, it is up to the client to integrate with Intent IQ. Having said that, our clients generally prefer to just use fresh data. Solutions Resources Company Contact Us California Privacy Notice The California Consumer Privacy Act provides California residents with certain rights concerning their Personal Information. A California resident can exercise certain rights under the CCPA, including: Request the personal information we collect about them. Ask that we delete the personal information we collect about them. Opt out of having their personal information sold (as defined in the CCPA). Kargo respects those rights and will honor CCPA requests made by a California resident or their authorized agent. Please note that, in providing advertising services to clients, we only collect the (1) Internet Protocol (IP) address associated with a user’s device and (2) the most recent search history associated with that IP address. We do not collect a user’s name, address, email address or similar personally identifiable information unless you choose to voluntarily provide us with such information through the Contact Us feature of the website. In order for Kargo to verify and process a CCPA request, Kargo will need to collect more Personal Information from the requestor than we collect in the course of verify your identity. Doing so will require us to collect more Personal Information from the requestor than we collect in the course of providing our advertising services. If you wish to proceed with a CCPA request: You must verify that you are a California resident. Please send a copy of proof of your California residency to CCPArequest@Kargo.com . The proof you submit should show your name and state of residence or California as the issuing state of the document (such as a driver’s license or state-issued ID card). We suggest you cross out any other identifying information (such as driver’s license number and street address) on the copy you submit. Your proof of California residency will be destroyed after it is reviewed and verified. If you are making the request on behalf of another person, provide proof of authorization to act on that person’s behalf pursuant to the CCPA. We may require the consumer to directly verify their identity with Kargo. You will receive a confirmation email once your California residency is confirmed. The email will include instructions on next steps to enable Kargo to determine whether any of your Personal Information resides in our records and to process your request. NOTE: After we process your request to opt out of the sale of your personal information, you may still see advertising served by Kargo. While you will not be served advertising based on your Personal Information, the advertising may be delivered to a general audience on the website you are using. How long does it take for my records to be removed? Once you receive an email from us confirming that we have processed your request, your record will be removed the next time our database updates. Most of the time, this should only take 24 hours. We strongly encourage you to verify that your information has been removed. If for some reason it has not, please call our support team at 1-800-301-5905 . How do I verify that my records were removed? Once you have received the email from us confirming that your information has been removed please wait at least 24 hours before checking for your records on our website. In some cases, you may need to "clear your cache/history" to ensure your computer is not storing and recalling information cached prior to the removal. We strongly encourage you to verify that your information has been removed. If for some reason it has not, please call our support team at 1-800-301-5905 . We will do everything in our power to ensure that your information stays out of our search results. Please be patient with us since we regularly update the Kids Live Safe Background Report search results from various public resources. When I remove my name from the Kids Live Safe database will data about me ever reappear in the Kids Live Safe search results again? We regularly update the Kids Live Safe Background Report search results from various public resources. Although we and our data partners do our best to suppress the records that you request to be removed from appearing in our search results, there may be times when our data partners provide us with new data about you that is different enough from the data you previously had removed – such as different spellings, initials, and/or addresses – that it is not possible to conclusively remove that new data. If you have previously been removed and see a new record about you appear in our Background Report search results, please repeat the removal process and we will remove that record as well. Mogean, Inc. ("Mogean", "we", "us") builds location data products: a dataset of United States places, and measurement services for out-of-home advertising. This policy covers www.mogean.com and Mogean's Exposure Measurement services. It is in three parts: the website , the POI dataset , and location data and the Exposure Measurement services . Purchases of the POI dataset happen at store.mogean.com and are governed by the Store privacy policy , which is a separate policy. Version 1.0. Effective date: September 30, 2026. Part A. This website www.mogean.com is an informational site. It sets no advertising cookies, and it collects no device identifiers and no location data. If you use the contact form or email us, we collect what you send: your name, work email address, company, and the contents of your message. We use it to reply to you, to answer questions about our products, and to keep a record of the exchange. We keep messages for as long as we need them to reply and for our business records. If we send you marketing email, every message carries a working unsubscribe link, and the opt-out page explains the other routes. Pages on this site link to other companies' websites; what those companies do with information is governed by their own policies, not this one. Part B. The POI dataset The POI dataset describes places, not people: names, addresses, coordinates, hours, categories, and operating status of United States places. It carries no device identifiers, no GPS traces, and no individual-level records, and it is built without location signals. Buying it is governed by the Store privacy policy . Part C. Location data and Exposure Measurement services This part covers the separate input behind Mogean's Exposure Measurement services. It is a different body of data from the POI dataset, held for a different purpose, and the POI dataset is never built from it. What data Mobile advertising identifiers — the resettable identifiers that mobile operating systems make available for advertising — and location signals associated with them: a coordinate, a timestamp, and technical attributes of the observation such as accuracy and the device's operating system. Where it comes from Mogean receives these signals under separate agreements covering their source, their permitted uses, and the opt-outs that must be honoured. Mogean does not collect them from this website. How it is used For out-of-home advertising clients, and for two jobs. The first is assembling exposed audiences: matching advertising screen interactions against device observations to identify the devices that could see a campaign. The second is foot traffic reports: measuring whether those devices later visited an advertiser's locations, and how much more often than a comparable unexposed group. The POI dataset supplies the context for that second job — which place a visit landed at, and what kind of place it is. How it is handled Inside the processing pipeline the signals are hashed. Where an exposed audience is delivered, it is delivered as standard mobile advertising identifiers, to the client who commissioned it, under a separate agreement that governs what the client may do with it. Foot traffic reports are delivered as aggregate results, not as device lists. How long it is kept Signals and identifiers are kept for as long as we need them to produce and support the measurement a client has commissioned, and then removed from the working data. A mobile advertising identifier submitted through the opt-out below is kept on the suppression list for as long as the list is used, so that the opt-out keeps being honoured. Who it is shared with Clients receive the outputs described above. Service providers — the vendors that host and process the data on our behalf — handle it under contract and for no purpose of their own. We may disclose information in response to a subpoena, court order, or other legal process, or where we believe disclosure is necessary to investigate or prevent illegal activity, fraud, or a threat to someone's safety. If Mogean is acquired or merged, or sells a business unit, information may transfer with it. Security We take steps to protect the information we hold from loss, misuse, unauthorised access, disclosure, alteration, and destruction. No set of measures can guarantee security. Children This site and these services are not directed to children under thirteen. If we learn that we hold information a child under thirteen gave us, we delete it promptly. Email is sufficient; no form is required. When a mobile advertising identifier is received, it is added to Mogean's deletion/suppression list and handled through the daily processing pipeline, after which it is excluded from the Exposure Measurement services. The opt-out page carries the same route. Your device also offers its own control: both major mobile operating systems let you reset the advertising identifier or turn off personalised advertising in the device settings. California and other state rights Residents of California and of other states with similar laws may ask what information we hold about them, ask for a copy, ask us to correct or delete it, and opt out of its sale or sharing. Use the same route: email info@mogean.com or privacy@mogean.com . We may need to ask for the identifier the request concerns before we can act on it, and exercising these rights costs you nothing. If a change materially affects what we do with information already collected, we will highlight it here. Adara provides digital advertising and analytics services for the benefit of our business customers, giving them the ability to reach and understand Internet users and consumers (like you) who are most likely to be interested in their respective products and services. Adara provides these services to customers such as website operators and mobile application developers (“Partners”). Consumers (like you) also benefit from Adara’s technology by receiving more relevant online marketing content: without our services you would still see ads online, but they would be less relevant to your interests. Here is a common example of how the Adara Platform can benefit you and our Partners: if you visit an airline or hotel website to book a flight or a hotel room and the airline or hotel website is an Adara Partner, then we will receive your search or booking travel intent about the destination including some related information (dates, class of travel, number of people traveling with you – for a full list see the Section below entitled “ What Personal Data Does Adara Collect?” ). text_excerpt: Your Privacy Choices StateCourts.org Home Inmate Search Contact Login Home Your Privacy Choices YOUR PRIVACY CHOICES You may have certain rights regarding our processing of your personal information under applicable law. If our processing of your personal information is governed by such laws, this page provides you with additional information regarding your rights related to your personal information under applicable local law. Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information You may have the right to opt out of the sale or sharing of your personal information. You may submit a request to confirm this or to formally exercise your rights using the form on our Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information page . Global Privacy Control We honor Global Privacy Control (GPC) opt-out signals. If we receive a GPC signal from your browser when you visit our services, we will treat it as an opt-out request from the sale or sharing of your personal information and a rejection of any non-necessary cookies. Covered Person Removal Request - Daniel Anderl Judicial Security and Privacy Act Under The Daniel Anderl Judicial Security and Privacy Act and any relevant federal and state laws, if you are a Covered Person—including, inter alia, current, former, or retired judges, prosecutors, law enforcement members, and their immediate family members living in the same household — and wish to have your details removed from our site, please contact us at privacy@statecourts.org . Please include your complete name, residence, and email address, as well as your status as a covered person. Ensure your email's subject line reads: "Attention Covered Person Removal Request." Your information will be used solely to process your privacy request efficiently. Expungement Records Please be aware that records that have been expunged, sealed, or otherwise restricted by a court order may still appear in our database as we aggregate information from publicly available sources. If you have questions regarding an expunged record appearing on our website, please submit your inquiry to privacy@statecourts.org with the subject line: "Attention Expungement Records." We will review your inquiry and respond in accordance with applicable law. Exercising Your Data Subject Rights These rights may apply in the following states: California, Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, Indiana, Iowa, Kentucky, Maryland, Minnesota, Montana, Nebraska, New Hampshire, New Jersey, Oregon, Rhode Island, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, and Virginia. Depending on where you live and subject to certain exceptions, you may have some or all of the following rights. Please note that exercising any of these rights will not result in any discriminatory treatment. Right to Know or Access. You have the right to ask whether your personal information is being processed and to request access to that information. Right to Correct. If any personal information we held about you is incorrect, you have the right to ask for it to be corrected or updated. Right to Delete. You may request the deletion of your personal information. Right to Data Portability. You have the right to receive your personal information in a portable, readily usable format that allows you to transfer it to another entity. Right to Know and/or Opt Out of Sale or Sharing. If your personal information is being sold to or shared with third parties, you have the right to know and to opt out such activities. Opt Out of Targeted Advertising. If your personal information is being used for targeted advertising, you may opt out of that use. Limit Use of Sensitive Personal Information. You may request that we limit the use or disclosure of your sensitive personal information to what is necessary to provide our services or as required by law. Disclosure of Third Parties. You may request a list of third parties that have received your personal information, along with the categories of information shared. Disclosure of Direct Marketers. You have the right to request the names and contact details of any third parties who have received your personal information for direct marketing purposes. Opt Out of Profiling. If your personal information is being used for profiling that could have legal or similarly significant effects on you, you have the right to opt out. Non-Discrimination. You have the right to use our services without being treated unfairly for exercising your privacy rights. We will not deny services, charge different prices, or provide a lower quality of service because you submitted a request. Appeals Request. If a request you previously submitted was denied, you have the right to appeal that decision. Appeals may be submitted to privacy@statecourts.org . To process your request, we may need to ask you additional questions to confirm the information associated with you. We will respond to your request within 45 days, or notify you if additional time is required. To submit a request to exercise any of the above rights, please contact us HERE © 2026 StateCourts.org. All Rights Reserved. To resolve disputes and enforce our agreements. To respond to law enforcement, governmental, or other legal requests and as required by applicable law. Merger, Sale, or Asset Transfer: We may disclose your personal information in connection with, or during negotiations of, any merger, sale of Steppingblocks’ assets, financing, or acquisition of all or a portion of our business by another company. For verification services. To protect the rights of Steppingblocks, its employees, service providers, assets, business, partners, or others. To respond to law enforcement, governmental, or other legal requests and as required by applicable law. We may disclose your personal information to our affiliates and subsidiaries, and to third parties who provide us with services to fulfill the purposes described in this policy. We may also disclose aggregated or de-identified personal information that cannot reasonably be used to identify you. We will not attempt to re-identify such information except as permitted by law. Steppingblocks Database We disclose personal information (name, email address, education, professional qualifications, work history, etc.) about profiles in our database with our business customers. We may also disclose your personal information for any other purpose with your consent or at your direction. We may sell or share your personal information. We may “sell” the following categories of personal information to third parties: (i) identifiers, such as your name, (ii) personal information described under certain state laws, (iii) characteristics of protected classification, such as age or gender, (iv) professional employment information, (v) education information, and (vi) inferences. We may sell or share your personal information for cross-context behavioral advertising purposes. We do not knowingly sell the personal information of minors under sixteen years of age. We do not sell your financial information when you make payments to us. We may retain your personal information in accordance with our legal obligations. We may retain your personal information for reasonable periods necessary to provide our services and for other disclosed purposes. Depending on where you reside, you may have rights regarding your personal information. Right to Notice. The right to notice about our collection, use, disclosure, sale, or sharing of information about you. Right to Know. The right to know if Steppingblocks possesses your personal information; and the right to know your personal information, including the specific pieces of personal information that we have about you and information about any automated decision-making, including profiling, about you made by steppingblocks.com. You may use this personal information request form to request access to your personal information. Right to Correct. The right to request that we correct your personal information. You may use this personal information request form to request correction of your personal information. Right to Restrict Use and Processing. You can request that we restrict the processing of your personal information. You may use this personal information request form to request restrictions on your profile processing. Right to Delete. The right to request that we delete the personal information we have collected about you. You may use this personal information request form to request the deletion of your personal information. In certain circumstances, laws may require that we retain personal information. Right to opt-out of sale/sharing/targeted advertising. You can opt out of the “sale,” “share,” or use of your personal information for targeted advertising. You may do so by using this personal information request form . In certain states, you may opt out of profiling in furtherance of decisions that produce legal or similarly significant effects and solely automated decisions. Limit the use of personal information and use of sensitive personal information. If you live in California, the right to ask us to limit our use of your personal and sensitive personal information. You may do so by using this personal information request form . Right to Data Portability. The right to obtain a copy of your personal information and profiling information that you may also request be transmitted to another entity. You may request information using this personal information request form. Non-Discrimination. You have the right not to receive discriminatory treatment for the exercise of your privacy rights under applicable law. Appeals. You have the right to request an appeal to Steppingblocks’ decision regarding your above rights by emailing privacy@steppingblocks.com . If you have concerns about the result of an appeal, you may contact the attorney general in the state where you reside. Non-retaliation. The right to be free from retaliation for exercising any of these rights. Sensitive and Demographic Personal Information. Steppingblocks makes certain inferences about individuals and stores that information in the database as disclosed above. This information may be considered “sensitive information” under certain states' privacy laws but is not sensitive information as defined by other states’ privacy laws because the information relates to individuals in their professional capacity rather than their consumer or household capacity. Cookies and Similar Tracking Technologies: steppingblocks.com uses cookies and similar tracking technologies to analyze visits to our websites and interactions with our communications to help us improve our website, services, and marketing campaigns. Most web browsers are set to accept cookies by default. If you prefer, you can usually adjust your browser settings to remove or reject browser cookies. Please note that removing or rejecting cookies could affect the availability and functionality of our services. Steppingblocks.com does not offer financial incentives for the collection, retention, or sale of personal information and does not have financial incentive programs for you to opt into. If you wish to exercise any of these privacy rights, please submit a request via the Privacy Form or via email at privacy@steppingblocks.com . In order to protect your personal information from unauthorized access or deletion, we may require you to verify your identity before we can process a privacy request related to your personal information. If we cannot verify your identity, we may be unable to comply with your request to provide, correct, or delete your personal information. You may have the right to designate an authorized agent to act on your behalf. You may have the right to designate an authorized agent to make a request on your behalf. We must receive a signed letter from you that describes you, your designated authorized agent, and the purpose of the designation. Your designated agent may then use the access, correction, deletion, and opt-out links described above to make a request on your behalf. In addition, we must still be able to verify your identity before you may access, correct, or delete your personal information. Disputes Regarding Our Privacy Practices If you have a dispute relating to our privacy practices, please email us at privacy@steppingblocks.com . How we protect your information. We have implemented security measures to help prevent unauthorized access to personal information. Despite these measures, no data transmission over the internet can be entirely secure, and we cannot guarantee or warrant the security of any information you transmit via our websites or apps. You are responsible for maintaining the security of your credentials used to access any Steppingblocks service or account, and you must report suspected unauthorized activity to us. We make reasonable efforts to restrict access to information to only those employees, contractors, and agents who need such access in order to operate, develop, improve, or deliver our programs, products, and services. We may revise this policy. We may update this policy in accordance with applicable law, including by posting a revised policy on the website that hosts this policy.
